text: its not that it doesnt refuse it its that its still wrong. make the cut, then look at where the verts land, its a lopsided cut
resolution: Confirmed the user's lopsided pyramid cut with numbers (proper repro on a SIDE triangle, sel:2 — earlier repros had accidentally hit the base): left slant edges cut level at exactly 1/3 and 2/3, right side cut at 0.3685, two verts dumped onto the base plane, and dir 0/1 produced byte-identical cuts (dead toggle). Root cause: the plane-comb fallback (the only path non-quad faces take) still aimed its planes with the req_2794 neighbor-normal average, which tilts on irregular neighborhoods; it survived the codex gate because the harness had no non-quad fixture (my spec's miss). Fix implemented directly: lcDeriveDirs reduced to the old studio's world-axis contract (axes flanking the selection normal's dominant axis — straight by construction; lcCanonSign + neighbor machinery deleted, ~115 lines), safe now because leaned/sheared quads ride the parametric ring and never touch the comb. Harness grew a pyramid fixture (16 rows): side-triangle loop cut asserts S=4, groups=13, and every new vert at a span-third fraction of a slant edge — the anti-lopsided contract. Gate (zig suites + 16-row parity + ship) running in background; commit follows its green.
